rationale: The profile is empty (no source lines, no function features), so this is a C++ benchmark of unknown internal structure — the safest strategy is a balanced table that enables all seven passes with no dimension dominating, letting per-function features drive selection rather than strong priors. SUB gets the highest SecurityGain since arithmetic substitution is uniformly applicable to C++ code and nearly risk-free. BCF and FLA carry the highest RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights (0.6-0.7) because bogus control flow and flattening are the most expensive transforms; their moderate-but-not-maximal SecurityGain weights let the feature-driven selector apply them only where the runtime/size budget per function justifies it. SPLIT is cheap and low-risk, serving as a diversity amplifier that composes well with FLA/BCF, so it stays enabled despite modest SecurityGain. ICALL's higher CorrectnessRisk (0.3) reflects indirect-call transformation interacting with C++ virtual dispatch and exception handling, so it is enabled but tempered. IBR and IGV provide inter-procedural/global diversity at moderate cost and are kept at mid-range weights. Overall: no pass is disabled, but the elevated cost weights on BCF/FLA ensure that on functions without favorable features the selector will skip the expensive transforms, keeping aggregate runtime and size overhead acceptable while preserving correctness.
